name: Vitess
model: Looks like one big MySQL database to the app; underneath, many ordinary MySQL servers, each holding some shards of the tables
engine_note: No storage engine of its own: a routing and management layer (vtgate, vttablet) over many MySQL/InnoDB servers (B+tree)
consistency: Full MySQL transactions inside one shard. Default cross-shard mode MULTI is best effort, not atomic; TWOPC mode makes cross-shard commits atomic but not isolated (fractured reads possible). Reads from MySQL replicas can be stale.
scaling: Sharding by a key you choose (a vindex), done and resharded online by Vitess; each shard is a MySQL primary with replicas.
reach: Reach for it when a MySQL app has outgrown one primary and you want to shard without rewriting it (Vitess served all YouTube traffic for years).
avoid: Avoid when you need atomic, isolated transactions across shards, or when one MySQL server is still enough (much more to operate).
escape: You leave the Postgres default for this because a MySQL app needs write sharding without a rewrite.
chat: Messages sharded by chat id for a very large MySQL-based chat product.
notes: Transaction modes quoted from the v24 distributed-transaction docs (default MULTI; TWOPC atomic but not isolated). Adopters per the v24 'What is Vitess' page: YouTube (all database traffic for over five years), Slack, Square, JD.com. PlanetScale also now offers Postgres (not Vitess-based); only its Vitess MySQL product counts here. CNCF graduated project.
